title: One question, reworded for each stage
statement: Differentiate by rewording one question over the same lines, knowledge and evidence, plainer for struggling readers and closer to the test for stronger ones, never by easier questions.
example: One worked example gives four versions of a question on the same lines, from plain wording through the state test's phrasing to a composition.
detail: A Grade 3 lesson design adds a second axis to its writing stages: the wording of the question changes while the core knowledge underneath stays identical, with the same lines, threshold and evidence and a different demand in the asking (`g9/library/text/L8d5159.txt`, line 43). Its worked example runs from a simplified floor with a plain verb, a plain noun and the line range spelled out, through the state test's phrasing, to a composition on the same lines and knowledge, and notes that the knowledge being tested does not move at all (lines 44-59). That gives a route down: a struggling child gets the simplified wording of the same question rather than an easier question, which keeps the class on one piece of knowledge (line 60).
against: A Grade 9 planning meeting floated a different route for first-timers, a glossary and "possibly an optional No Fear Shakespeare-style side-by-side modern translation "for like a stage one learner … somebody who's really struggling"." (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/MEETING-2026-10-01.md`, lines 41-43). Another record keeps a level's difficulty out of hard syntax and reworded easier lessons, while part of this design's change between stages is a change of wording (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, line 59).

evidence.quote: Same lines, same threshold, same evidence, different demand in the asking.
A child who is struggling can be given the simplified wording of the same question rather than an easier question, which keeps the class on one piece of knowledge.
Same lines, same knowledge, a composition instead of an answer.
The knowledge being tested does not move at all.
